Before diving into each meaning, here's the one idea that ties everything together:

"Bulk" always revolves around the concept of large size, large volume, or large quantity.

If you hold onto this core idea, every meaning of the word will feel natural and connected.
Meaning 1: The Large Physical Size or Mass of Something

This is the most visual meaning. When you say something has bulk, you mean it takes up a lot of physical space — it is large, heavy, or thick in a way that is noticeable.

Think of a huge wardrobe being moved through a narrow hallway. The problem is its bulk — it is simply too big, too heavy, too space-consuming to fit easily.

Examples:

  • The bulk of the old ship made it hard to navigate through the canal.
  • He was a man of considerable bulk — tall, wide, and heavily built.
  • The sofa's bulk meant that three people had to carry it.

Key feeling of this meaning: You're talking about something's physical bigness — the sheer size and weight that makes it impressive, difficult to handle, or hard to ignore.
Meaning 2: The Majority — "The Bulk of Something"

This is the most commonly used meaning in everyday reading and conversation. Here, "the bulk of" is a phrase that simply means "the greatest part of" or "most of."

You are not talking about physical size here. You are talking about proportion — how much of something belongs to one category compared to the rest.

Think of a pie. If you cut it and one person gets 80% of it, that person has the bulk of the pie.

Examples:

  • The bulk of the students passed the exam. (= Most of the students passed.)
  • She spent the bulk of her savings on the trip. (= She spent most of her savings.)
  • The bulk of the work was done by Tuesday. (= The greater part of the work was finished.)
  • The bulk of his speech was about the economy. (= Most of his speech covered the economy.)

Key feeling of this meaning: You could almost always replace "the bulk of" with "most of" and the sentence would mean the same thing. However, "the bulk of" sounds slightly more formal and precise, and it also carries a subtle sense of weight or heaviness — like you're emphasizing just how large that majority really is.
Meaning 3: In Bulk — Large Quantities (Especially When Buying or Selling)

When goods or items are bought, sold, or stored in bulk, it means they are dealt with in very large amounts, usually without individual packaging, and often at a lower cost per unit.

Imagine a restaurant that buys rice. Instead of buying small 1 kg bags like a household would, they buy a 50 kg sack all at once. They are buying in bulk.

Examples:

  • It's cheaper to buy washing powder in bulk.
  • The factory orders its raw materials in bulk to reduce costs.
  • They shipped the grain in bulk — no boxes, no bags, just loose grain poured into the cargo hold.

Key feeling of this meaning: The emphasis is on large quantity at once, usually for economic or practical reasons. Buying in bulk saves money. Shipping in bulk saves packaging. The word suggests efficiency through sheer volume.
Meaning 4: Body Mass — Size and Muscle (Fitness Context)

In the context of the human body, bulk refers to the large physical size of a person, especially muscle mass. When someone is described as having bulk, they appear big, muscular, and physically powerful.

Examples:

  • The rugby player had impressive bulk — his arms were enormous.
  • He had the speed of a sprinter but the bulk of a weightlifter.
  • She admired his bulk, the result of years of training.

You will also hear the phrase "add bulk" or "put on bulk", meaning to build muscle and increase body mass.

  • He was eating more protein to add bulk before the competition.
  • The trainer told her to lift heavier weights if she wanted to put on bulk.

Key feeling of this meaning: This is about the body being impressively large and solid — not just fat, but powerful physical size. It carries a sense of strength and physical presence.
Meaning 5: Cargo and Goods (Specialized / Commercial Use)

In trade and shipping, bulk refers to goods that are loose and unpackaged — transported in large amounts directly, without individual containers. Think of coal, wheat, oil, or sand being poured directly into a ship's storage area.

Examples:

  • The ship was carrying bulk cargo — mostly grain and coal.
  • The port specializes in handling bulk goods.

This meaning is most common in business, logistics, and trade contexts. You are unlikely to use it in everyday conversation, but you may encounter it in articles about shipping, commerce, or manufacturing.
How to Know Which Meaning Is Being Used

Since "bulk" has multiple meanings, here's a simple way to figure out which one applies:

  • If someone is describing the physical size or heaviness of an object or person → Meaning 1 or 4
  • If the phrase is "the bulk of" followed by a noun → Meaning 2 (the majority of something)
  • If the phrase is "in bulk" → Meaning 3 (large quantities, buying/selling)
  • If the context is shipping or trade and the word is used alone → Meaning 5
Common and Important Phrases to Know

These phrases are so frequently used that you should learn them as complete units:

  • The bulk of → the greatest part of something (The bulk of the damage was in the north.)
  • In bulk → in large quantities (Buying in bulk saves money.)
  • In bulk (shipping) → loose, unpackaged goods (The wheat was transported in bulk.)
  • Add/put on bulk → build body size/muscle (He's trying to put on bulk.)
  • Sheer bulk → emphasizing how large something is (The sheer bulk of the machine was staggering.)
  • The bulk → used alone, meaning "the larger part" (The bulk remains unfinished.)

——

Here is everything pulled together simply:

Bulk as a noun has one soul — largeness. Depending on the context, it describes:

  1. The large physical size or mass of an object or person.
  2. The majority or greatest portion of something (always in the phrase "the bulk of").
  3. Large quantities of goods, typically bought, sold, or stored all at once (always in the phrase "in bulk").
  4. Muscular body mass — how physically large and solid a person is.
  5. Loose, unpackaged goods in trade and shipping.

No matter which meaning you encounter, you can always trace it back to that one simple idea: something that is large in size, amount, or quantity. That's the heart of the word.
